cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Database replication keeps copies of data on multiple nodes by shipping each change from one node to the others. Any setup can be described as Topology (who), Timing (when), Payload (what) and Delivery (how).

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Single-leader avoids write conflicts. Multi-leader accepts writes on several nodes and needs conflict resolution. Leaderless writes to W and reads from R replicas with R + W > N so they overlap. Synchronous waits for the replica before acking; asynchronous does not. Payload can be statements, rows, logical records or physical WAL.

questions.q: If the database is replicated, do you still need backups?
questions.a: Yes. Replicas apply mistakes like DELETE without WHERE within milliseconds.

questions.q: Why must R + W > N in leaderless replication?
questions.a: So every read quorum overlaps at least one node with the latest write.

questions.q: What is the main challenge of multi-leader?
questions.a: Write conflicts when two leaders change the same data at once.
